svg.title: Dizziness: first decide whether it is true vertigo; non-vestibular dizziness has organic and psychiatric causes, while peripheral vertigo is named by how long attacks last and whether hearing is affected: BPPV, Meniere's disease, vestibular neuronitis or labyrinthitis, superior canal dehiscence, and aminoglycoside toxicity; the vestibular group box explains how the inner ear signals movement and a shared exam box reads the nystagmus; each column gives presentation, investigations and treatment

svg.text: "Dizzy": is it TRUE VERTIGO, an illusion of rotary movement?

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: history is 80% of the workup · exam: nystagmus (named by its FAST phase) and ataxia · CT, MRI

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: balance: vestibular + vision + position sense → brainstem, cerebellum → eye and limb muscles

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: one ear fails → imbalance read as rotation: eye muscles = NYSTAGMUS · higher centres = VERTIGO · limbs = ataxia · vagal

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif
Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: anxiety: often the cause OR the effect · vestibular schwannoma: one-sided hearing loss + tinnitus, rarely vertigo

svg.text: episodic, limited duration · hearing symptoms · nausea, vomiting, sweating, bowels · worse with head movement

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: • hair cells (CN VIII): bending toward the kinocilium opens K+ channels → depolarizes

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: • resting firing ~100/s, so each afferent signals BOTH directions

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: • otoliths (utricle, saccule): linear movement, tilt vs gravity · posture

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: • canals: rotation · endolymph lags, pushes the cupula · gaze stabilization

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: • canals work in PAIRS: the brain reads the difference, so one dead ear = false rotation

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: • VOR: 3 neurons, eyes compensate in 10-15 ms

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif
Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: • slow phase = vestibulo-ocular reflex · fast phase = saccade that resets the eye

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: • PERIPHERAL (spontaneous vestibular): direction FIXED, mostly horizontal, SUPPRESSED by fixation

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif
Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: • caloric COWS: Cold → fast phase Opposite, Warm → Same · tests the brainstem in coma (needs the MLF for conjugate eyes)

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: • other pathologic: positional · gaze-paretic · rebound · fixation · congenital · dissociated

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: How long does an attack last, and is hearing lost?

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: seconds: BPPV, dehiscence · minutes to hours: Ménière's (hearing lost) or migrainous (hearing kept) · days: labyrinthitis (hearing lost) or neuronitis (kept) · forever:
